items.title: Live: Yelling heard in Victorian Labor meeting as caucus devolves into chaos, interim leader named
items.description: Premier Jacinta Allan pulls out of the race after facing a challenge for leadership of the Victorian Labor Party from her deputy Ben Carroll. Follow our live coverage.

items.title: Who is the man who wants to be Victoria's 50th premier?
items.description: Former lawyer and political adviser Ben Carroll is vying to become Victoria's new premier, four months out from the state election.

items.title: Breaking: Origin Energy believes 900,000 customers' data accessed in breach
items.description: Origin Energy says it started reviewing a "potential security threat" early this month but deemed it not credible, before new information indicated a breach.

items.title: Live: Origin shares dive on data breach details, ASX down as oil price plunges
items.description: Shares in energy giant Origin are down after it provided an update on its data breach, while the Australian share market is lower after oil prices plunged more than 9 per cent overnight. Follow live.

items.title: Salmon farming transformed Norway. Now it's facing the consequences
items.description: Norway's salmon industry is a global behemoth 18 times the size of Tasmania's. But the country's success holds a warning for Australia.

items.title: Secret documents show 'horrifying' traces of horse meat in food
items.description: Government documents show hundreds of businesses operating in Australia have breached food safety laws, with one politician warning "you could be eating a minced horse".

items.title: Science and politics collide in fraught puberty blockers debate
items.description: The fierce debate over puberty blockers has become a collision of science and politics. To try to address a fractured consensus, the federal government is attempting to lay the groundwork for a national standard.

items.title: Live: Penny Wong signals fuel excise cut will 'discontinue' after August 2
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong has signalled the fuel excise discount will "discontinue" after August 2. Follow live.

items.title: The 'strange, anomalous, anachronistic' Commonwealth Games
items.description: The Commonwealth Games continues to roll on despite calls to decolonise our lives, with Scotland of all places a strange venue to stage two celebrations of the British Empire over the past 12 years.

items.title: Quick hits: Davies makes history, Diamonds clap back in uni debate
items.description: Rose Davies runs a "race of a lifetime" to make Australian history, and the Diamonds remain in the spotlight even off the court. Here are the quick hits from day four of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: US and Iran in 'good talks' Trump says as support for war wanes
items.description: US President Donald Trump says the United States is having "good talks" with Iran, and there is a chance of a deal over their conflict, but he warns that US strikes will resume if the negotiations fail to deliver.

items.title: Thrice-bankrupt builder's past catches up with him in small town
items.description: Unregistered builder Steve Preston has been operating in New South Wales after falling foul of authorities in Western Australia and Queensland.

items.title: AFL clubs explore facial recognition as new ticketing method
items.description: Facial recognition technology is being used as an alternative form of ticketing, but some experts are concerned it could open the door to the data being used for more than just event entry.

items.title: What to expect from antisemitism royal commission in coming weeks
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is continuing in Sydney, with witnesses to give evidence about ways to improve education and training to prevent hate.

items.title: Oscar-winning composer brings Icelandic poetry to Australian stages
items.description: Oscar-winning composer Hildur Guðnadóttir never imagined global fame. Now she's written new music for the Australian Chamber Orchestra, inspired by Icelandic poetry.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in the ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned; we might try to trick you.

items.title: Struggling to save? Here are five ways to curb your impulse spending
items.description: If you'd rather be saving than shopping, but are struggling to switch gears, there are ways to change your habits.

items.title: How an accident changed the path of a grieving Angus Taylor
items.description: The Liberal leader opens about a balcony fall that left him with a broken back and altered the course of his life.

items.title: Twin tragedies leave community, nursing colleagues in shock
items.description: The car crash death of mother-of-two Elaine Gee and the stabbing of another woman will send "ripples" through the Tasmanian community, a family violence support service says.

items.title: Search resumes for missing baby off South East SA coast
items.description: SA Police hold grave fears for the safety of a baby missing after the bodies of a woman and toddler were recovered in waters off Port MacDonnell.

items.title: Singer D4vd to stand trial for allegedly killing and dismembering 14yo girl
items.description: D4vd, the 21-year-old singer born David Burke, will stand trial charged with killing and dismembering 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez.

items.title: Australia should brace for war impact to get worse, Treasury warns
items.description: The federal government is yet to reveal whether it will extend the fuel excise discount, which is set to expire this week.

items.title: Trump tips the balance towards China in trade war
items.description: China has the market sewn up in everything from solar panels to battery manufacturing and wind turbines. And now it is challenging America's commanding role in technology.

items.title: Savannah Guthrie pleads with mother's kidnappers to 'help us find her'
items.description: US TV show host Savannah Guthrie makes an emotional plea to her mother's kidnappers, asking them to "tell us where to look for her".

items.title: Warnings consumers 'the fall guy' if data centres soak up spare power supply
items.description: Consumers should brace for hefty increases in the cost of generating electricity as data centres suck up vast quantities of power faster than new plants can be built, experts say.
